newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand bonds close weaker on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand bonds close weaker on profit taking.

text.p: 0500 GMT
* New Zealand bonds weaken on profit taking
* Short-end hangs in with support from the TWI
* SEK two-year Eurobond issued overnight
* Cash at 9.95 pct vs 9.90 pct at Monday's close
* 90 day bills 9.97 pct vs 9.97
* 7/98 bond yields 8.18 vs 8.13
* 02/01 bond yields 8.38 vs 8.33
* 11/06 bond yields 8.38 vs 8.33
* Sept bill futures 90.07 vs 90.10, vol 604
New Zealand bonds closed weaker on Tuesday on profit taking and weakening sentiment related to the October 12 general election.
The 7/98 bonds were particularly vulnerable to a squeeze dealers said.
One said the spreads versus the U.S. in the long end had come back to 135-140 basis points from 190 a couple of months ago and it was now looking like a a good reverse trade.

"A lot of offshore guys got into the kiwi-U.S. around that 190-200 level. I think people are starting to take a little bit of profit from that offshore...especially with the lead-up to the election just around the corner," he said.
The short end remained stuck around 10 percent, helped by a firmer Trade-Weighted Index which lifted to 65.54 from 65.30.
The 90-day bills are seen locked in a 9.80-10.0 percent range.

The market is anticipating the Reserve Bank will maintain the status quo on September 13 when it releases its next set of economic forecasts. It will emphasise its ability to ease at a later date but it may be concerned that recent cuts in mortgage interest rates will reignite the housing market, a dealer said.
The bank may also be concerned that lower confidence levels are the result of the impending election rather than higher interest rates, and confidence may soon rebound.
The 8.40 percent level is seen as an important support technical level for the long bonds and it would take a big surge to breach that.
-- Simon Louisson 64 4 4734 746
